summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, poorly controlled HIV/AIDS, and recent MRSA bacteremia presented with a two-day history of worsening headache, neck stiffness, photophobia, and shortness of breath following a missed dialysis session. Initial concerns for meningitis were raised, but the patient declined a lumbar puncture. Empiric antibiotics and antivirals were started, though subsequent negative blood cultures and a negative serum cryptococcal antigen made infectious causes unlikely. Symptoms improved with hemodialysis and supportive care, and were attributed to a severe headache episode possibly exacerbated by missed dialysis, post-herpetic neuralgia, and medication rebound. Oral vancomycin for C. difficile was discontinued as diarrhea had resolved. Warfarin was held due to a supratherapeutic INR and restarted at a lower dose. Hypercalcemia was noted and managed with cinacalcet and withholding vitamin D. The patient was discharged home with services on a short course of pain medication, with plans for outpatient follow-up for HIV adherence support, ophthalmology, and cardiac monitoring.
problems: Herpes zoster with other nervous system complications
Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Nephritis and nephropathy, not specified as acute or chronic, with unspecified pathological lesion in kidney
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
